title: Residue fields of finite type schemes have finite transcendence degree
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme [def-weil-scheme-over-base, def-pc-scheme] of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $x\in X$. Then the transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree] $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)$ of the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] is finite.

source.place: Lemma \"lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring\" (Tag 00P0), applied to A/p on an affine neighbourhood of x

proof.text: Let f be the structure morphism X -> Spec K and give kappa(x) its K-algebra structure via f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x. The map K -> (f x).asIdeal.ResidueField is essentially of finite type by the Mathlib ideal residue-field instance (RingHom.essFiniteType_algebraMap and instance search). The inverse of Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso is essentially of finite type since it is a surjective ring map, using RingHom.FiniteType.of_surjective and RingHom.FiniteType.essFiniteType.

LocallyOfFiniteType.stalkMap f x says the stalk map is essentially of finite type; RingHom.EssFiniteType.residueFieldMap gives the same property on residue fields. Compose this map with the two maps of step 1 using RingHom.EssFiniteType.comp. Their composite is definitionally f.residueFieldAlgebraMap x, so kappa(x) is an Algebra.EssFiniteType K algebra with precisely the structure in the theorem.

The instance in Mathlib.FieldTheory.FinTrdeg turns Algebra.EssFiniteType K (X.residueField x) into FinTrdeg K (X.residueField x). Apply trdeg_lt_aleph0 K (X.residueField x) to get the required strict cardinal inequality. This uses the existing Mathlib finite-transcendence-degree API directly and does not choose a transcendence basis. Quasi-compactness is not needed in this local argument; the original signature is unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00P0 affine residue-field argument and Fields Tag 030F; implemented by H1 on 2026-10-16 using Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType.stalkMap, RingHom.EssFiniteType.residueFieldMap and trdeg_lt_aleph0. The three-map essential-finiteness argument also occurs in the proved library theorem closedPoint_iff_residueField_trdeg_zero_and_finite.
